blocks.text: A CHECK constraint gives a rule for stored data. The database rejects a row when that rule is false.
Use the SQL Run button for examples marked runnable. They use this site's in-browser SQLite database and sample-only table names. A Python example needs Python on your own computer instead.

blocks.title: Protect a positive number

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `NOT NULL` requires a value to be present. It is a separate rule from numeric range checks.
`CHECK` tests a stored value against a rule, such as a non-negative count. Use NOT NULL too when missing values are forbidden.
`SELECT` names the output values. `AS` can give a calculated result a readable column name.

blocks.text: The sample value 5 is accepted. A negative points value would fail the check.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: CHECK alone does not replace NOT NULL when a missing value must also be refused.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Explain why both NOT NULL and CHECK are useful.
